summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on dialysis, mechanical aortic valve, peripheral vascular disease, and recent left toe amputation was admitted for hypoxia and altered mental status. She had worsening shortness of breath and was found to be volume overloaded, with pulmonary edema contributing to low oxygen levels. Her confusion was attributed to polypharmacy, particularly from opioids and sedating medications. Dialysis successfully removed excess fluid, improving oxygenation. Mental status normalized after discontinuing lorazepam, gabapentin, and ropinirole, and reducing OxyContin from 30 mg to 20 mg twice daily. A weaning plan was established for further opioid reduction. She was stabilized on increased labetalol for blood pressure control, and sodium thiosulfate was restarted. With resolved symptoms and stable vitals, she was discharged home with home health services and follow-up plans.
